To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the majority of older adults with depression in primary care are untreated, that the majority of those who receive treatment receive it from the primary care physician, that the majority are treated in a substandard manner, and that the majority of the untreated and the suboptimally treated patients are not aware that they are receiving substandard care.

the prevalence of depression was higher in the oldest-old than in the younger elderly, that depression was associated with functional impairment in the oldest-old but not in the younger elderly (in the latter, depression was associated with social impairment), and that the prevalence of major depression in the oldest-old was similar to that found in other studies, whereas the prevalence of minor depression was lower.
